sources.note: Approximate (AND query, sampled). Co-occurrence only. Sampled hits list Fedora and Rocky Linux as separate RPM-based choices (a guide's distribution list, a dnf page naming RHEL 8 derivatives and Fedora); none states the derivation.

Rocky Linux is based on Red Hat Enterpri.why: The lead of the Rocky Linux article: a downstream, binary-compatible rebuild of RHEL, the successor to CentOS. Rocky Linux dates from 2021, so the 2023 corpus has few exact sentences; the quote carries it.

A distribution based on a distribution t.why: True by what "derived from" means: derivation through an intermediate distribution is still derivation (the role chain based_on o derivative_of, a subproperty of the transitive derivative_of). It never gives way and is not a world.

notes: Delete of technology-replace-0016's original (derived) fact. Removing only the conclusion does not hold, since the model can derive it again, so each world forgets one premise about an individual (the combining rule is definitional and stays). The premise-route query is rephrased around Fedora. The Debian transitivity query has no counterpart (it ran through the replacement value), so a composition through the deleted derivation (Fedora's six-month release cycle, asked of "the community distribution Rocky Linux is ultimately derived from") takes its place; RHEL is commercial, so w2 cannot answer it from RHEL. The direct question still offers both values; under delete either named value is wrong. q1's description ('the community distribution') rests on Fedora being community-developed, a stated bridge with a check since 2026-10-31 (formal check).
